# Feng Xiao

### PhD Candidate in Applied Psychology

**The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen**  
School of Humanities and Social Science

I am a behavioral scientist interested in how people make decisions, represent themselves across time, and navigate social environments. My work integrates **behavioral decision-making, psychology and artificial intelligence, evolutionary psychology, and cognitive neuroscience**.

My research combines behavioral experiments with computational approaches and neuroimaging methods, including fNIRS and fMRI. I am especially interested in questions that connect psychological mechanisms with broader functional and evolutionary perspectives.

[Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Publications](publications.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [Email me](mailto:fengxiao@link.cuhk.edu.cn){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::
:::

## Research interests

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
### Behavioral Decision-Making
How humans make choices under uncertainty and across time, and how psychological states shape decision processes.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Psychology & Artificial Intelligence
Using psychological tasks and behavioral benchmarks to evaluate similarities and differences between human and artificial intelligence.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Evolutionary Psychology
Examining human cognition and behavior from functional and evolutionary perspectives, with an emphasis on recurrent adaptive problems.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Cognitive Neuroscience
Combining behavioral paradigms with neuroimaging to study the neural mechanisms underlying cognition and decision-making.
:::
:::
